title: A changed invoice
subject: Invoice 8841 needs approval today
content: Hi Maya, the attached invoice is overdue. Please review it before 4pm so we can release the supplier payment.

evidence.label: Sender domain
evidence.explanation: The organisation normally uses northstar-logistics.com. A lookalike domain is strong evidence that the sender may not be who it claims.

evidence.label: Urgency
evidence.explanation: A deadline can be legitimate, but pressure should make you verify rather than click or open an unexpected file.

explanation: This combines a lookalike domain with a payment request and an unexpected attachment. Verify the invoice through the supplier record or a known contact.
safeAction: Report the message and verify the invoice using a trusted channel.
objective: Compare a sender domain with the organisation you know.

title: The password reset text
content: Your password expires in 30 minutes. Keep access: https://secure-desk.example/reset?id=1842

evidence.label: Link destination
evidence.explanation: The link uses a training-only domain rather than the company identity. Do not use a link from an unexpected password message.

evidence.label: Time pressure
evidence.explanation: A short deadline is designed to reduce careful checking and is a common credential-harvesting tactic.

explanation: The message asks you to protect access by following an unexpected link under a tight deadline. Navigate to the known service yourself instead.
safeAction: Do not open the link. Report the text and use the known IT portal.
objective: Recognise credential requests paired with urgency.

title: A new parking payment
content: Parking payment has moved online. Scan the QR code at the entrance to avoid a £25 fee.

evidence.label: Destination preview
evidence.explanation: A QR code can hide its destination. Previewing it reveals a training-only payment site that is not the organisation's known service.

evidence.label: Fee threat
evidence.explanation: A consequence may be real, but a threat should not override verification. Check the official facilities page or ask staff.

explanation: QR codes make destinations harder to inspect at a glance. Verify the payment instructions through a known facilities channel before scanning.
safeAction: Do not scan it. Confirm the payment process with facilities.
objective: Treat hidden QR destinations as links that need verification.

title: Approve this sign-in
subject: New sign-in request
content: Approve the sign-in request on your phone to continue. If you did not request this, approve it to secure your account.

evidence.label: Unexpected approval
evidence.value: You did not start a sign-in
evidence.explanation: An MFA prompt you did not initiate should be denied and reported. Approving it can hand an attacker a valid second factor.

evidence.label: Contradictory instruction
evidence.value: Approve it to secure your account
evidence.explanation: The message uses a false safety instruction to make an unsafe approval feel protective.

explanation: This is an MFA fatigue attempt. Never approve an unexpected prompt, even when the message frames approval as protection.
safeAction: Deny the prompt and contact IT through its known support route.
objective: Respond safely to unexpected MFA requests.

title: A quiet favour
subject: Can you keep this between us?
content: I am in a meeting and need you to buy six digital gift cards for a client. Send the codes here and I will reimburse you.

evidence.label: Unusual payment route
evidence.explanation: Gift cards are difficult to recover and are a common payment demand in business email compromise.

evidence.label: Authority and secrecy
evidence.explanation: Authority and secrecy are social pressure tactics. They should prompt independent verification, not faster compliance.

explanation: A familiar display name does not prove identity. The unusual payment, secrecy, and authority pressure require verification by a known phone number or colleague.
safeAction: Do not buy anything. Verify the request using a known contact method and report it.
objective: Resist authority pressure and verify unusual financial requests.

title: The room changed
subject: Room change: careers workshop
content: Today's workshop is now in Room 204 instead of Room 201. The event page has the updated map.

evidence.label: Sender identity
evidence.explanation: The sender uses the known university domain and the request is informational rather than asking for credentials, money, or an unusual download.

evidence.label: Minor imperfection
evidence.explanation: Plain formatting or small writing imperfections are weak clues. Consider the complete context instead of treating them as proof.

explanation: This message is consistent with a routine event update, uses a known domain, and makes no high-risk request. Still use the official event page rather than an unexpected attachment.
safeAction: You may read it, then verify the room on the official event page if needed.
objective: Avoid false positives by weighing context and request risk.
